intended_object: The canonical morphism of fppf sheaves of groups over S from the fppf quotient sheaf G/H to the sheaf represented by Q, induced by a homomorphism q : G → Q of S-group schemes whose kernel is H. Inferred from the docstring and from the lemmas relativeFppfQuotientMk_comp_map and relativeFppfQuotientMap_isIso that use it.
explanation: The body takes the pointwise map G(T)/H(T) → Q(T) built with QuotientGroup.lift (yonedaQuotientMap). This is well defined because the pullback (kernel) hypothesis gives range i_T ≤ ker q_T. The body then lifts group values one universe up and extends across sheafification with Mathlib's sheafifyLift, using that Q's functor of points is an fppf sheaf. By the universal property of sheafification, the result is the unique sheaf morphism whose composite with the quotient projection is the morphism represented by q; this is proved in relativeFppfQuotientMk_comp_map. That is the standard induced map G/H → Q. The kernel hypothesis is stronger than strictly needed (it suffices that q kills H), but the library already has that general version as relativeFppfQuotientLift. This definition is the kernel-specific comparison map used to prove G/H ≅ Q, and its docstring says so. The setting (fppf topology on Over S, group objects) is the natural one.
